scenes.title: Hook: spray ring astern
scenes.picture: Frame 0, mid dolly-in at 35 mm, Kai centred at the tiller. His face is lit warm-red by his headlamp, the one practical light carrying the night, and his eyes are locked on the glowing compass. Over his right shoulder, on the starboard quarter, a moonlit spray ring is already spinning on the black-teal water. He does not turn. The 'WATERSPOUT IN THE DARK' kinetic title runs for 2.5 s. A high orbit then holds as the ring widens astern while Kai keeps facing the bow. This is the threat-reveal plant, the hero not looking, held for at least 3 s.

scenes.title: Alone in the Triangle
scenes.picture: Aerial pullback at 21 mm from the sloop's single warm headlamp point to an empty, moon-silvered sea with no other lights to any horizon. The moon sits frame-left as the geography anchor. The spray ring is still a faint pale disc astern. Far off on the frame-right horizon, behind the boat, the squall line's cloud base flickers once.

scenes.title: Jacket on the hook, radio glow
scenes.picture: Truck right at 50 mm past the companionway. A yellow-orange life jacket with its tether coiled through the D-ring hangs on a brass hook, which plants the climax-solving gear at 6 s. The VHF's green display reads 16. Kai rubs his eyes under the headlamp and taps the chartplotter. Behind him, through the cockpit opening, lightning silently backlights the squall line, which he cannot see.

scenes.title: Thunder: clock starts
scenes.picture: A low 35 mm angle. Thunder rolls and Kai's head snaps up toward the bow, where the lightning line now rakes the sky ahead. The SQUALL ETA badge slams in at 08:00. He is still facing away from the spray ring astern.

scenes.title: Reach for the engine
scenes.picture: Kai lunges across the cockpit to the engine panel, follow-tracking at 28 mm, and twists the key. The amber panel lights wink on. Over his bent back, through the stern rail, the spray ring has grown and spiral bands curl on the water.

scenes.title: Reserved close-up: engine dies, he turns
scenes.picture: A silent 75 mm extreme close-up on Kai's face. The panel lights die and the engine coughs out. A hiss rises and his eyes move, then his head turns slowly toward the stern. The headlamp beam swings with him. This is the reserved hero close-up, with no words.

scenes.title: POV: the spray ring
scenes.picture: A 110 mm POV from the cockpit with subtle handheld. A tight white collar of spray whirls on the water a few boat-lengths astern, and a faint condensation finger dips from the cloud above it. The headlamp beam just reaches the spray.

scenes.title: Run downwind
scenes.picture: Kai hauls the tiller to windward and the mainsail and jib snap full. Follow-track at 28 mm alongside the heeling sloop as foam pours off the bow, with the spout trailing frame-left astern.

scenes.title: The lead never grows
scenes.picture: An over-the-shoulder shot at 50 mm. Kai glances back twice and the spout is the same size in frame both times, its spray ring thicker. The SQUALL badge ticks to 05:00.

scenes.title: Tiny sloop, darkening sky
scenes.picture: A silent low reveal at 24 mm from wave level. The tiny sloop, with one warm headlamp point, sits under a lowering, bruised cloud base as the music riser swells. The moon is now veiled frame-left.

scenes.title: Midpoint: mature vortex
scenes.picture: A lightning flash. Crane rise at 21 mm reveals a full vortex column from boiling sea to cloud that towers over the sloop, the mast a thin line beside it. The spout now matches the squall wall behind it, lit blue-white.

scenes.title: Knuckles on the tiller
scenes.picture: A thunder crack lights Kai's face at 85 mm with the vortex looming out of focus behind him. A slow push in down to his knuckles whitening on the tiller as his eyes search the dark for another way.

scenes.title: Boiling base
scenes.picture: A low reveal at 110 mm on the vortex base, where a ring of sea is torn into a sheeting cylinder of spray and debris foam flung outward. Its rotation is evident.

scenes.title: Step one: jacket and tether
scenes.picture: A STEP 1 badge slams in. Kai rips the life jacket off the companionway hook and shrugs it on, then snaps the tether carabiner onto the jackline with a visible click. The SQUALL badge reads 03:00. Spray whips past the headlamp beam.

scenes.title: Step two: read its track
scenes.picture: A STEP 2 badge. Kai sights the spout against the starboard shroud wire, then a POV at 110 mm shows the funnel sliding steadily left relative to the shroud as the camera drifts.

scenes.title: Reserved decision close-up
scenes.picture: A silent 75 mm close-up of Kai's jaw setting, then his arm throws the tiller hard over. The tiller creaks. There are no words.

scenes.title: Step three: beam-on, it passes
scenes.picture: A STEP 3 badge. Orbit clockwise at 24 mm as the sloop swings beam-on and the wake bends into a right angle. The vortex slides past the stern on its own line while spray sheets across the cockpit and Kai hunches on his tether.

scenes.title: Decay
scenes.picture: Astern, the funnel ropes out thin, bends and frays into drifting mist. The spray ring collapses to flat water, with the sloop small and intact frame-right.

scenes.title: Squall slams in
scenes.picture: A rain wall hits the sloop and knocks it onto its ear. The SQUALL badge hits 00:00 in a whip.

scenes.title: Riding it on the tether
scenes.picture: Handheld shot of Kai thrown against his taut tether as the jib tears. The rain-streaked chartplotter shows the boat icon inside the Triangle's dashed outline.

scenes.title: Right-angle wake
scenes.picture: Kai exhales as the rain eases. Aerial at 24 mm over the dark sea where the sloop's foam wake shows a sharp 90-degree bend, then the shot holds as the rain lifts and the moon reappears frame-left.

scenes.title: Sting: he looks back
scenes.picture: Kai, soaked and centred at the tiller, glances back over his shoulder into the dark stern quarter as his headlamp beam sweeps the water.

scenes.title: Loop frame
scenes.picture: The frame-0 composition returns: the dark starboard quarter behind Kai, a wave slap, then a hard cut back into the hook.
